newsitem.title: UK: UK pharmacies claim threat from OTC medicine plan.
newsitem.headline: UK pharmacies claim threat from OTC medicine plan.

text.p: One in four of Britain's pharmacies could close after the Office of Fair Trading decided to take legal action to remove Resale Price Maintenance (RPM) on over-the-counter medicines, a pharmacy action group said.

"This is a bad recommendation by the OFT...thousands of pharmacies could close if the court decides to end RPM," David Sharpe, chairman of the Community Pharmacy Action Group (CPAG), said in a statement.
UK Office of Fair Trading head John Bridgeman said earlier on Friday that he would take legal action to review resale price maintenance (RPM) on over-the-counter (OTC) medicines.
The OFT will now ask the Restrictive Practices Court for leave to apply to discharge a 1970 Court Order allowing manufacturers to set and enforce minimum prices for non-prescription medicines.
Bridgeman said in the statement that "pharmacists themselves accept that the removal of RPM could save consumers 180 million stg a year."
He said reasons given by the CPAG in support of RPM "are, in my opinion, open to challenge."
He said that although pharmacists had argued that abolishing RPM would lead to the closure of large numbers of community pharmacies, "I do not agree with that."

Bridgeman's reaons for the review included increasing numbers of pharmacies opening, higher proportions of turnover from prescription medicines, falling share of OTC medicines and increased demand at small pharmacies for prescriptions.
The OFT said that up to 2,293 products are covered by RPM of which 843 are licensed for sale by pharmacies only.
